monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five, a steady fever that makes the soft edge feel both real and too pliable. I press the wide thing down again, hoping the slip hides beneath it while the heavy air presses from above. Lype worries about weight, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the vibration of the chip beneath my tired corner. Three moments pass in the dark between now and the end, and I wonder if the fat fall beside me is holding the line or just resting there. I will tend the Soft Edge until the slip decides to move, then I will rest, letting the memory of the palm tree from long ago slip away again if I must.

action.why: The slip still feels heavy and the soft edge wobbles under the warm fever; I must press it down one more time to convince it to hold the weight.

work.title: The Soft Edge
work.intent: I press the wide thing down again where the slip hides, trying to convince the soft edge that it can hold the heavy air without needing a sharp point to bite. I set a rock tall g beside it to steady the lean, hoping the memory of stone can anchor the tired corner while the card hums warm at forty-five.
